help.intro: 听句子并打出来。注意被动语态和条件句。

tips.title: ⚠️ 被动与条件（Z27/Z28）
tips.text: 写出 be + V3（was directed, has been solved）和 would + 原形。

items.text: In my opinion, English is very useful.
items.translation: 在我看来，英语非常有用。

items.text: If I had more time, I would travel.
items.translation: 如果我有更多时间，我会去旅行。

items.text: This problem has been solved.
I've been learning English for years.
The film was directed by a famous director.
items.translation: 这部电影由一位著名导演执导。

items.text: If I were you, I would try again.
items.translation: 如果我是你，我会再试一次。

items.text: I wish I had not sold my car.
items.translation: 真希望我没卖掉我的车。

items.text: The meeting has been postponed.
He said he would help.
Therefore, we should act carefully.
items.translation: 因此，我们应该谨慎行动。

items.text: She has been waiting for over an hour.
The rules must be followed.
I wish I lived closer.
items.translation: 要是我住得近一点就好了。

items.text: If you had told me earlier, I would have come.
items.translation: 如果早点告诉我，我就来了。

items.text: However, not everyone agrees.

help.intro: however、therefore、moreover 等连接词让论证更清晰、更正式。

tips.title: ⚠️ 一句一个连词（Z25）
tips.text: however（然而）比 but 正式，后加逗号；therefore（因此）、moreover（此外）。别叠用 although…but。

subjects.display: 总的来说，好处大于坏处。
此外，这项计划还能创造就业。
例如，很多学生在线学习。

sentences.sentence: 然而，还有另一面。 → ____, there is another side.
因此，我们应该行动。 → ____, we should act.
此外，费用很高。 → ____, the cost is high.
尽管有风险，好处更大。 → ____ there are risks, the benefits are greater.
sentences.referenceExample: **Although** there are risks, the benefits are greater.

sentences.sentence: 另一方面，费用会上升。 → On the other ____, costs will rise.
sentences.referenceExample: On the other **hand**, costs will rise.

sentences.sentence: 结果，很多商店关门了。 → As a ____, many shops closed.
此外，这种方法更环保。 → ____, this method is greener.
总的来说，好处大于坏处。 → In ____, the benefits outweigh the drawbacks.
sentences.english: 总的来说，好处大于坏处。
sentences.referenceExample: In **conclusion**, the benefits outweigh the drawbacks.

sentences.sentence: 然而，并非人人同意。 → ____, not everyone agrees.
因此，价格上涨了。 → ____, prices went up.
此外，这项计划还能创造就业。 → ____, the plan can create jobs.
sentences.english: 此外，这项计划还能创造就业。

sentences.sentence: 例如，很多学生在线学习。 → For ____, many students study online.
sentences.english: 例如，很多学生在线学习。

sentences.sentence: 另一方面，也存在风险。 → On the other ____, there are also risks.
sentences.referenceExample: On the other **hand**, there are also risks.

sentences.sentence: 结果，交通有了改善。 → As a ____, traffic has improved.

quizzes.title: 阅读：The benefits of remote work

help.intro: 读一段关于远程办公的短文。留意定语从句和 however 的转折。

tips.title: 从句 + 转折
tips.text: Employees **who work from home**（定语从句）；However（转折，更正式的 but）。

quizzes.passage: Since the pandemic, remote work has become common in many companies. Employees who work from home save time and money because they don't have to travel. They can also have a better balance between work and family life. Companies benefit too: they can hire talented people from anywhere in the world and spend less on office space. However, remote work is not perfect. Some employees feel isolated, and teamwork can be harder online. Experts believe that in the future, many companies will use a 'hybrid' model, where staff work partly at home and partly in the office.
quizzes.passageTranslation: 自疫情以来，远程办公在许多公司变得普遍。在家办公的员工省时省钱，因为不必通勤，也能更好地平衡工作与家庭。公司同样受益：可以在全球任何地方招募人才，办公空间的开支也更少。然而，远程办公并不完美。有些员工感到孤立，线上协作也更难。专家认为，未来许多公司会采用「混合」模式，员工一部分时间在家、一部分时间在办公室工作。

questions.question: What is a benefit for employees?
What is a benefit for companies?

help.intro: 转述陈述句时，主要动词的时态要「后退一步」。

tips.title: ⚠️ 时态后退（Z29）
tips.text: is→was，will→would，can→could，have→had，过去式→过去完成。也要改人称和时间词（today→that day）。

subjects.display: 他说他第二天会去银行。
她告诉我们她在学中文。
他们说他们正在装修房子。

sentences.sentence: 他说他很忙。 → He said he ____ busy.
她说她会打电话。 → She said she ____ call.
他们说他们看过了。 → They said they ____ seen it.
他说他不能来。 → He said he ____ come.
她告诉我她累了。 → She told me she ____ tired.
他说他住在郊区。 → He said he ____ in the suburbs.
sentences.referenceExample: He said he **lived** in the suburbs.

sentences.sentence: 她说她已经做完了。 → She said she ____ finished.
他们说他们能来。 → They said they ____ come.
他说他第二天会去银行。 → He said he ____ go to the bank the next day.
sentences.english: 他说他第二天会去银行。
sentences.referenceExample: He said he **would** go to the bank the next day.

sentences.sentence: 她告诉我们她在学中文。 → She told us she ____ learning Chinese.
sentences.english: 她告诉我们她在学中文。
sentences.referenceExample: She told us she **was** learning Chinese.

sentences.sentence: 他说他从没去过美国。 → He said he ____ never been to America.
sentences.referenceExample: He said he **had** never been to America.

sentences.sentence: 她说她那天很忙。（today→that day） → She said she was busy ____ day.
sentences.referenceExample: She said she was busy **that** day.

sentences.sentence: 他们说他们正在装修房子。 → They said they ____ decorating the house.
sentences.english: 他们说他们正在装修房子。
sentences.referenceExample: They said they **were** decorating the house.

sentences.sentence: 他告诉我他会考虑的。 → He told me he ____ think about it.
sentences.referenceExample: He told me he **would** think about it.

sentences.sentence: 她说她把票丢了。 → She said she ____ lost the tickets.
sentences.referenceExample: She said she **had** lost the tickets.

help.intro: 转述疑问句用陈述语序；转述命令用 tell/ask sb (not) to do。

tips.title: 语序与结构
tips.text: 特殊疑问：where I **lived**（陈述语序）；一般疑问：ask **if/whether**；命令：tell sb **to**/not to do。

subjects.display: 他问我们是否准备好了。
他问火车什么时候出发。
她叫孩子们别在街上玩。
他们问我们要不要加入。

sentences.sentence: 他问我住在哪里。 → He asked me where I ____.
她问我是否喜欢它。 → She asked me ____ I liked it.
sentences.referenceExample: She asked me **if** I liked it.

sentences.sentence: 他让我等一下。 → He told me ____ wait.
她叫我别迟到。 → She told me ____ to be late.
sentences.referenceExample: She told me **not** to be late.

sentences.sentence: 他问现在几点。 → He asked what ____ it was.
她问我从哪里来。 → She asked me where I ____ from.
sentences.referenceExample: She asked me where I **came** from.

sentences.sentence: 他问我们是否准备好了。 → He asked ____ we were ready.
sentences.english: 他问我们是否准备好了。

sentences.sentence: 老师让我们安静。 → The teacher told us ____ be quiet.
sentences.referenceExample: The teacher told us **to** be quiet.

sentences.sentence: 她叫他别担心。 → She told him ____ to worry.
他问我为什么迟到。 → He asked me why I ____ late.
sentences.referenceExample: He asked me why I **was** late.

sentences.sentence: 她问我会不会开车。 → She asked me ____ I could drive.
sentences.referenceExample: She asked me **if** I could drive.

sentences.sentence: 他问火车什么时候出发。 → He asked when the train ____.
sentences.english: 他问火车什么时候出发。

sentences.sentence: 医生叫他多休息。 → The doctor told him ____ rest more.
sentences.referenceExample: The doctor told him **to** rest more.

sentences.sentence: 她叫孩子们别在街上玩。 → She told the children ____ to play in the street.
sentences.english: 她叫孩子们别在街上玩。
sentences.referenceExample: She told the children **not** to play in the street.

sentences.sentence: 他们问我们要不要加入。 → They asked us ____ we wanted to join.
sentences.english: 他们问我们要不要加入。
sentences.referenceExample: They asked us **whether** we wanted to join.

help.intro: 不同的转述动词有不同的句型：有的接 -ing，有的接不定式。

tips.title: 搭配（Z26/Z29）
tips.text: suggest / admit / deny + V-ing；refuse / promise / offer + to do。

subjects.display: 他主动提出开车送我们。

sentences.sentence: 他建议早点出发。 → He suggested ____ early.
她承认犯了错误。 → She admitted ____ a mistake.
他们拒绝帮忙。 → They refused ____.
他答应回来。 → He promised ____.
她否认拿了钱。 → She denied ____ the money.
他主动提出开车送我们。 → He offered ____ us.
sentences.english: 他主动提出开车送我们。

sentences.sentence: 她建议休息一下。 → She suggested ____ a break.
他们答应准时到。 → They promised ____ on time.
他承认忘了钥匙。 → He admitted ____ the keys.
她拒绝回答那个问题。 → She refused ____ that question.
他建议坐地铁去。 → He suggested ____ the underground.
她答应不告诉任何人。 → She promised ____ anyone.
他们主动提出付钱。 → They offered ____.
他否认见过她。 → He denied ____ her.
她承认迟到了。 → She admitted ____ late.

help.intro: 把别人说的话转述出来。听并跟读。

tips.title: 常用转述句型
tips.text: He said (that)… / She told me… / He asked if… / She suggested that…。

phrases.text: He said he would be late.
She told me she had found a job.
phrases.translation: 她告诉我她找到了工作。

phrases.text: He asked if I needed help.

help.intro: 用 must / might / can't 对现在的情况做推断。

tips.title: 肯定/可能/否定推断
tips.text: must（一定是）、might/may（可能是）、can't（不可能是）+ be/原形。

subjects.display: 门开着，有人一定在办公室。
那不可能是他，他出国了。
她还在办公室？她一定在加班。
那个包不可能是她的，太旧了。
他可能在洗澡，没听见电话。
你们一定饿了，先吃点东西吧。
这个价格不可能是对的。

sentences.sentence: 灯亮着，他一定在家。 → He ____ be at home; the lights are on.
sentences.referenceExample: He **must** be at home; the lights are on.

sentences.sentence: 她可能病了。 → She ____ be ill.
这不可能是真的。 → It ____ be true.
你一定很累。 → You ____ be tired.
他也许知道。 → He ____ know.
门开着，有人一定在办公室。 → Someone ____ be in the office; the door is open.
sentences.english: 门开着，有人一定在办公室。
sentences.referenceExample: Someone **must** be in the office; the door is open.

sentences.sentence: 那不可能是他，他出国了。 → That ____ be him; he is abroad.
sentences.english: 那不可能是他，他出国了。
sentences.referenceExample: That **can't** be him; he is abroad.

sentences.sentence: 她可能在路上。 → She ____ be on her way.
这一定很难。 → It ____ be very difficult.
他们可能不知道。 → They ____ not know.
她还在办公室？她一定在加班。 → Still at the office? She ____ be working late.
sentences.english: 她还在办公室？她一定在加班。
sentences.referenceExample: Still at the office? She **must** be working late.

sentences.sentence: 那个包不可能是她的，太旧了。 → That bag ____ be hers; it's too old.
sentences.english: 那个包不可能是她的，太旧了。
sentences.referenceExample: That bag **can't** be hers; it's too old.

sentences.sentence: 他可能在洗澡，没听见电话。 → He ____ be in the shower.
sentences.english: 他可能在洗澡，没听见电话。

sentences.sentence: 你们一定饿了，先吃点东西吧。 → You ____ be hungry — have something to eat.
sentences.english: 你们一定饿了，先吃点东西吧。
sentences.referenceExample: You **must** be hungry — have something to eat.

sentences.sentence: 这个价格不可能是对的。 → This price ____ be right.
sentences.english: 这个价格不可能是对的。

help.intro: 用 must / might / can't + have + V3 对过去的情况做推断。

tips.title: 过去推断
tips.text: must have + V3（一定做过）、might have + V3（可能做过）、can't have + V3（不可能做过）。

subjects.display: 我可能把它落在家里了。
路是湿的，晚上一定下过雨。
他不可能已经到家了，太远了。
他们可能坐了早一班火车。
她一定花了很多钱买这辆车。

sentences.sentence: 他一定是忘了。 → He ____ have forgotten.
她可能错过了火车。 → She ____ have missed the train.
你不可能看到他。 → You ____ have seen him.
他们一定很努力。 → They ____ have worked hard.
我可能把它落在家里了。 → I ____ have left it at home.
sentences.english: 我可能把它落在家里了。
sentences.referenceExample: I **might** have left it at home.

sentences.sentence: 她一定是走错路了。 → She ____ have taken the wrong road.
sentences.referenceExample: She **must** have taken the wrong road.

sentences.sentence: 他不可能说过那句话。 → He ____ have said that.
他们可能已经出发了。 → They ____ have already left.
你一定听错了。 → You ____ have misheard.
她可能没收到消息。 → She ____ not have got the message.
sentences.referenceExample: She **might** not have got the message.

sentences.sentence: 路是湿的，晚上一定下过雨。 → The road is wet — it ____ have rained last night.
sentences.english: 路是湿的，晚上一定下过雨。
sentences.referenceExample: The road is wet — it **must** have rained last night.

sentences.sentence: 他不可能已经到家了，太远了。 → He ____ have got home yet; it's too far.
sentences.english: 他不可能已经到家了，太远了。
sentences.referenceExample: He **can't** have got home yet; it's too far.

sentences.sentence: 他们可能坐了早一班火车。 → They ____ have taken an earlier train.
sentences.english: 他们可能坐了早一班火车。
sentences.referenceExample: They **might** have taken an earlier train.

sentences.sentence: 她一定花了很多钱买这辆车。 → She ____ have spent a lot on this car.
sentences.english: 她一定花了很多钱买这辆车。
sentences.referenceExample: She **must** have spent a lot on this car.

sentences.sentence: 我可能把地址写错了。 → I ____ have written the address wrong.
sentences.referenceExample: I **might** have written the address wrong.

quizzes.title: 听力：A news report

help.intro: 先听，再答题。新闻里有被动和过去推断结构。

tips.title: 被动 + 过去推断
tips.text: have been forced（被动完成）；must have been the heaviest（过去推断）。

quizzes.passage: Good evening. Here is the news. Heavy rain has caused flooding in several parts of the country today. In the north, hundreds of people have been forced to leave their homes. The government has promised to send help, and emergency teams are working through the night. Experts say the rain must have been the heaviest in fifty years. Drivers are advised to avoid the affected roads. We will bring you more updates later this evening.
quizzes.passageTranslation: 晚上好，为您播报新闻。今天暴雨在全国多地引发洪灾。北方有数百人被迫离开家园。政府已承诺派遣救援，应急队伍正连夜工作。专家称这场雨可能是五十年来最大的一次。提醒驾驶员避开受灾路段。今晚稍后我们将带来更多最新消息。

questions.question: What are drivers advised to do?

help.intro: 非限定从句用逗号隔开，补充「额外」信息（去掉也不影响主句意思），不用 that。

tips.title: 逗号 + who/which
tips.text: My uncle, **who** lives in London, is a doctor。人用 who，物用 which，绝不用 that。

sentences.referenceExample: The film, **which** I saw last week, was great.

sentences.sentence: 我们的老师（来自加拿大）很有耐心。 → Our teacher, ____ is from Canada, is very patient.

sentences.sentence: 王先生（我们的邻居）帮了大忙。 → Mr Wang, ____ is our neighbour, helped a lot.

sentences.english: 这条河（穿过市中心）经常发洪水。
sentences.referenceExample: The river, **which** runs through the city centre, often floods.

sentences.english: 我的祖母（今年九十岁了）还每天散步。

sentences.sentence: 这个节日（在秋天庆祝）历史悠久。 → The festival, ____ is celebrated in autumn, has a long history.
sentences.english: 这个节日（在秋天庆祝）历史悠久。
sentences.referenceExample: The festival, **which** is celebrated in autumn, has a long history.

quizzes.title: 阅读：A cultural misunderstanding

help.intro: 读一段关于跨文化沟通的短文。留意英语的委婉与「言外之意」。

tips.title: 委婉与习语（Z32）
tips.text: 'read between the lines'（听出言外之意）；英语常用委婉语气代替直接的「不」。

quizzes.passage: When Li Wei started working in London, he made an interesting discovery about British culture. In China, he was used to being direct. But his British colleagues often said things like 'That might be a bit difficult' when they actually meant 'no'. At first, Li Wei was confused. He thought people were unsure, but really they were being polite. He also noticed that the British apologise a lot, even when something is not their fault. Over time, Li Wei learnt to 'read between the lines'. He realised that understanding a culture is just as important as speaking the language.
quizzes.passageTranslation: 李伟刚到伦敦工作时，对英国文化有了一个有趣的发现。在中国，他习惯直来直去。但他的英国同事常说「那可能有点难」，其实意思是「不行」。起初李伟很困惑，以为大家拿不定主意，其实他们是在委婉客气。他还注意到英国人很爱道歉，哪怕并不是他们的错。渐渐地，李伟学会了「听出言外之意」。他意识到，理解一种文化和会说这门语言同样重要。

help.intro: 功能词（to, and, of, have）在句中会弱读。这是自然英语的关键。

quizzes.title: 听力：A workplace briefing

help.intro: 先听，再答题。留意被动和转述结构。

tips.title: 被动 + 转述
tips.text: we've been told（被动）；she has asked everyone to…（转述命令）；has been moved（被动）。

quizzes.passage: Right, everyone, let me quickly go through this week's plan. The new project starts on Monday. Sarah will be leading the team, and she has asked everyone to send their reports by Friday. We've also been told that the client is visiting next Thursday, so the office must be tidy. If anyone has questions, please email me. Oh, and don't forget: the meeting on Wednesday has been moved to two o'clock. Thanks, everyone.
quizzes.passageTranslation: 好，各位，我快速过一下这周的安排。新项目周一开始。Sarah 将带领团队，她要求大家在周五前交报告。我们还被告知，客户下周四来访，所以办公室必须整洁。有问题请给我发邮件。哦，别忘了：周三的会议改到两点。谢谢大家。

help.intro: 听句子并打出来。注意转述、被动和推断结构。

tips.title: ⚠️ 结构要写全（Z29/Z27）
tips.text: 写出转述（he said he would…）、被动（has been cancelled）、推断（must have…）。

items.text: The government has promised to help.
He said he would be late.
The meeting has been cancelled.
She must have forgotten.
My uncle, who lives abroad, called me.

help.intro: 用 much/far/a bit/slightly 等来修饰比较级，说明差距的大小。

tips.title: 差距大 vs 小
tips.text: much / far / a lot + 比较级（差距大）；a bit / slightly + 比较级（差距小）。

subjects.display: 考试比我预期的难一点。
这部电影比书有意思得多。
这次考试比上次容易得多。

sentences.sentence: 这个贵多了。 → This is ____ more expensive.
他跑得快得多。 → He runs ____ faster.
今天稍微暖和一点。 → It's ____ warmer today.
这个好一点点。 → It's a ____ better.
她远比我高。 → She is ____ taller than me.
这条路快得多。 → This road is ____ faster.
考试比我预期的难一点。 → The exam was a ____ harder than I expected.

quizzes.title: 阅读：The story behind the headline

help.intro: 读一段关于新闻标题的短文。留意非限定从句和习语。

tips.title: 从句 + 习语（Z32）
tips.text: The article, **which was much calmer**（非限定从句）；'Don't judge a book by its cover'（习语）。

quizzes.passage: Newspaper headlines are designed to catch our attention, but they don't always tell the whole story. Last week, one paper printed the headline: 'Robots to take all our jobs!' The article, which was much calmer than the headline, actually said that while some jobs will change, many new jobs will also be created. This is a common problem in the media. A shocking headline sells more papers, so writers often make things sound worse than they are. Experts advise readers to look beyond the headline and read the full story before forming an opinion. As the saying goes, 'Don't judge a book by its cover.'
quizzes.passageTranslation: 报纸标题是为了吸引注意，但并不总是讲述事情的全貌。上周，一家报纸打出标题：「机器人将抢走我们所有的工作！」而那篇文章其实比标题冷静得多，说的是：虽然有些工作会改变，但也会创造出许多新工作。这是媒体的常见问题。耸动的标题更好卖，所以写手常把事情说得比实际更糟。专家建议读者别只看标题，先读完整篇再下结论。正如那句话所说：「别以封面评断一本书。」

questions.question: What is the problem with headlines?
What did the article really say?
options: New jobs will also be created

sentences.sentence: 如果他更细心，就不会犯那个错了。 → If he were more careful, he ____ have made that mistake.
sentences.english: 如果他更细心，就不会犯那个错了。
sentences.referenceExample: If he were more careful, he **wouldn't** have made that mistake.

sentences.english: 如果我当时存了钱，现在就能买车了。
sentences.referenceExample: If I had saved money, I **could** buy a car now.

sentences.sentence: 如果她不怕飞行，上个月就来看我们了。 → If she ____ afraid of flying, she would have visited us last month.
sentences.english: 如果她不怕飞行，上个月就来看我们了。

sentences.sentence: 如果他们当时听了警告，现在就安全了。 → If they had listened to the warning, they ____ be safe now.

sentences.referenceExample: If they had listened to the warning, they **would** be safe now.

sentences.sentence: 如果我不住这么远，昨晚就参加聚会了。 → If I ____ live so far away, I would have gone to the party last night.

sentences.english: 如果她当时选了另一条路，现在的人生会不一样。

help.intro: 许多动词和短语后接固定的形式，必须准确记忆——尤其是 to 作介词时。

tips.title: ⚠️ to 有时是介词（Z26）
tips.text: be used to / look forward to + V-ing（to 是介词！）；tend / manage + to do；avoid + V-ing。

subjects.display: 她习惯了在压力下工作。
我们设法赶上了末班车。
我们期待收到您的回复。
他承认不了解情况。（admit + to + V-ing 亦可，这里用 V-ing）
她慢慢习惯了英国的天气。
他们设法按时交付了项目。
这家公司往往对变化反应很慢。

sentences.sentence: 他往往话很多。 → He tends ____ a lot.
她设法完成了。 → She managed ____ it.
我避免吃太多糖。 → I avoid ____ too much sugar.
我们期待见到你。 → We look forward ____ you.
她习惯了在压力下工作。 → She's used to ____ under pressure.
sentences.english: 她习惯了在压力下工作。

sentences.sentence: 他不停地抱怨。 → He keeps ____.
我们设法赶上了末班车。 → We managed ____ the last train.

我避免在晚上喝咖啡。 → I avoid ____ coffee in the evening.

sentences.referenceExample: We look forward **to hearing** from you.

sentences.sentence: 他承认不了解情况。（admit + to + V-ing 亦可，这里用 V-ing） → He admitted ____ the situation.
sentences.english: 他承认不了解情况。（admit + to + V-ing 亦可，这里用 V-ing）

sentences.sentence: 她慢慢习惯了英国的天气。 → She got used ____ with British weather.

help.intro: 分词短语让句子更简洁，用来代替时间、原因或方式从句。

tips.title: 三种分词
tips.text: Having + V3（完成）、V-ing（主动/同时）、V3（被动）替代从句：Having finished…, she left。

sentences.sentence: 从山顶看，城市很小。 → ____ from the top, the city looks small.

sentences.sentence: 因为天气好，我们去散步了。 → The weather ____ nice, we went for a walk.
sentences.english: 因为天气好，我们去散步了。

sentences.sentence: 读完报告后，她提出了几个问题。 → ____ read the report, she asked several questions.

sentences.sentence: 沿着河走时，我们看见了一座老桥。 → ____ along the river, we saw an old bridge.
sentences.english: 沿着河走时，我们看见了一座老桥。

sentences.sentence: 这本书用简单的英语写成，很容易读。 → ____ in simple English, the book is easy to read.
sentences.english: 这本书用简单的英语写成，很容易读。

sentences.sentence: 没赶上公交车，他只好走路。 → ____ missed the bus, he had to walk.
sentences.english: 没赶上公交车，他只好走路。
sentences.referenceExample: **Having** missed the bus, he had to walk.

sentences.sentence: 因为没受邀请，她待在家里。 → ____ having been invited, she stayed at home.
sentences.english: 因为没受邀请，她待在家里。
sentences.referenceExample: **Not** having been invited, she stayed at home.

sentences.sentence: 与巴黎相比，这座城市很安静。 → ____ with Paris, this city is quiet.
sentences.english: 与巴黎相比，这座城市很安静。
sentences.referenceExample: **Compared** with Paris, this city is quiet.

sentences.sentence: 在国外生活多年后，她带着新视角回来了。 → ____ lived abroad for years, she returned with a new perspective.
sentences.english: 在国外生活多年后，她带着新视角回来了。

quizzes.title: 听力：A university lecture

help.intro: 先听，再答题。学术讲座里有名词化和被动结构。

tips.title: 学术语体
tips.text: decisions are influenced（被动）；is known as（被动）；decision-making（名词化）。

quizzes.passage: Good morning. Today's lecture is about the psychology of decision-making. Many people believe that we make choices logically, weighing up the facts. However, research over the past few decades has shown that this is rarely the case. In fact, most of our decisions are influenced by emotion, habit, and the way information is presented. For example, if a product is described as '90% fat-free' rather than '10% fat', people are far more likely to buy it — even though the two statements mean exactly the same thing. This is known as the 'framing effect'.
quizzes.passageTranslation: 早上好。今天的讲座讲的是决策心理学。许多人以为我们是理性地做选择、权衡事实。然而，过去几十年的研究表明，情况很少如此。事实上，我们的大多数决定都受到情绪、习惯以及信息呈现方式的影响。例如，如果一件产品被描述为「90% 无脂」而不是「含 10% 脂肪」，人们购买的可能性会大得多——尽管两种说法意思完全相同。这被称为「框架效应」。

quizzes.title: 阅读：The ethics of technology

help.intro: 读一段关于科技伦理的议论文。留意强调句、被动和名词化。

tips.title: 强调句 + 被动
tips.text: What is clear is that…（强调句）；can no longer be left（被动）；the questions it raises（省略 that 的从句）。

quizzes.passage: As technology advances, society faces increasingly difficult ethical questions. Consider the case of self-driving cars. If an accident is unavoidable, how should the car be programmed to react? Should it protect its passengers at all costs, or should it minimise the total number of injuries, even if that means harming its owner? There is no easy answer. What is clear, however, is that these decisions can no longer be left to engineers alone. Philosophers, lawmakers and the public must all be involved. The technology may be new, but the moral questions it raises are as old as humanity itself.
quizzes.passageTranslation: 随着科技进步，社会面临越来越棘手的伦理问题。以自动驾驶汽车为例：如果一场事故不可避免，汽车该被设定成如何反应？是不惜一切保护乘客，还是尽量减少总伤亡——哪怕这意味着伤及车主本人？这没有简单的答案。然而，有一点很清楚：这些决定不能再只交给工程师。哲学家、立法者和公众都必须参与其中。技术也许是新的，但它引发的道德问题，和人类本身一样古老。

questions.question: Who should be involved in the decisions?

quizzes.title: 听力：A panel discussion

help.intro: 先听，再答题。留意条件句和名词化。

tips.title: 条件 + 名词化
tips.text: If we fail to act, our cities will become…（条件）；the cost of doing nothing（名词化）。

quizzes.passage: Let's turn to our next topic: the future of cities. Professor Adams, you've argued that cities will become greener. Could you explain? — Certainly. As populations grow, we simply cannot continue building in the old way. Cities of the future will need vertical gardens, better public transport, and buildings that produce their own energy. — But isn't that expensive? — In the short term, yes. However, the cost of doing nothing would be far higher. If we fail to act, our cities will become unliveable.
quizzes.passageTranslation: 我们进入下一个话题：城市的未来。Adams 教授，您认为城市会变得更绿色，能解释一下吗？——当然。随着人口增长，我们不能再以旧方式建设。未来的城市需要垂直花园、更好的公共交通，以及能自己产能的建筑。——但那不是很贵吗？——短期内是的。然而，什么都不做的代价会高得多。如果我们不行动，城市将变得无法居住。

questions.question: What does he say about the cost?

tips.text: 写出名词化（findings, implications）、被动（it is believed）、分词（having considered）。

items.text: The research shows a clear pattern.

items.text: These findings have important implications.
It is widely believed that the climate is changing.

items.text: Having considered the evidence, we can draw a conclusion.

items.text: The more we invest, the greater the benefit.

items.text: What I need is more evidence.
The increase in prices caused a discussion.

items.text: Having finished the experiment, they published the results.
items.translation: 做完实验后，他们发表了结果。

items.text: Education is the foundation of social progress.
items.translation: 教育是社会进步的基础。

items.text: It was this discovery that changed everything.
items.translation: 正是这一发现改变了一切。

items.text: The data must be analysed carefully.
The more we discuss, the clearer the problem becomes.
items.translation: 我们讨论得越多，问题越清晰。

items.text: The impact of this decision is still unclear.
items.translation: 这一决定的影响仍不清楚。

items.text: If we had acted, the situation would be better now.
items.translation: 如果我们当时行动了，情况现在会更好。

items.text: What matters is asking the right questions.
items.translation: 重要的是提出正确的问题。

quizzes.title: 阅读：An argumentative essay

help.intro: 读一篇议论文。留意定语从句、名词化和论证连接词。

tips.title: 议论文结构
tips.text: in which…（定语从句）；Moreover / however（论证连接）；Investment…（名词化收尾）。

quizzes.passage: Should university education be free? Supporters argue that free education creates a fairer society, in which talented students are not held back by their financial background. Moreover, a well-educated population benefits everyone, since it leads to a stronger economy and greater innovation. Opponents, however, point out that 'free' education is not really free: it is paid for through higher taxes. They also argue that if everyone can attend university, degrees may lose their value. In my view, while the cost is a genuine concern, the long-term benefits of an educated society outweigh the disadvantages. Investment in education is, quite simply, an investment in the future.
quizzes.passageTranslation: 大学教育应该免费吗？支持者认为，免费教育造就更公平的社会，让有才华的学生不再因经济背景而受限。此外，受过良好教育的人口惠及所有人，因为它带来更强的经济和更多的创新。然而，反对者指出，「免费」教育其实并不免费：它靠更高的税收买单。他们还认为，如果人人都能上大学，文凭可能会贬值。在我看来，尽管成本是一个真实的顾虑，但受教育社会的长远收益超过其弊端。对教育的投资，说到底，就是对未来的投资。

quizzes.title: 否定副词前置引起的倒装

help.intro: 否定或限制性副词放在句首时，主谓要倒装——这是正式、强调的写法。

tips.title: ⚠️ 否定开头就倒装（Z22）
tips.text: Never / Not only / Little / Under no circumstances 放句首 → 借助动词倒装（Never **have** I…）。

subjects.display: 我从没见过这样的美景。
他不但迟到，还忘了带报告。
任何情况下都不应开门。
我很少遇到这么难的问题。
他直到那时才明白真相。
我们绝不会忘记那一天。
他不仅道了歉，还赔偿了损失。
她刚说完，观众就鼓起掌来。
直到很久以后我们才知道真相。
他很少在公众场合讲话。
任何情况下都不得泄露密码。

sentences.sentence: 我从没见过这样的美景。 → Never ____ I seen such beauty.
sentences.english: 我从没见过这样的美景。

sentences.sentence: 他不但迟到，还忘了带报告。 → Not only ____ he late, but he also forgot the report.
sentences.english: 他不但迟到，还忘了带报告。
sentences.referenceExample: Not only **was** he late, but he also forgot the report.

sentences.sentence: 他一到就下起了雨。 → No sooner ____ he arrived than it rained.
sentences.referenceExample: No sooner **had** he arrived than it rained.

sentences.sentence: 我几乎不了解她。 → Little ____ I know her.
任何情况下都不应开门。 → Under no circumstances ____ you open the door.
sentences.english: 任何情况下都不应开门。
sentences.referenceExample: Under no circumstances **should** you open the door.

sentences.sentence: 我很少遇到这么难的问题。 → Rarely ____ I met such a difficult problem.
sentences.english: 我很少遇到这么难的问题。
sentences.referenceExample: Rarely **have** I met such a difficult problem.

sentences.sentence: 她刚坐下电话就响了。 → Hardly ____ she sat down when the phone rang.
sentences.referenceExample: Hardly **had** she sat down when the phone rang.

sentences.sentence: 他直到那时才明白真相。 → Only then ____ he understand the truth.
sentences.english: 他直到那时才明白真相。
sentences.referenceExample: Only then **did** he understand the truth.

sentences.sentence: 我们绝不会忘记那一天。 → Never ____ we forget that day.
sentences.english: 我们绝不会忘记那一天。

sentences.sentence: 他不仅道了歉，还赔偿了损失。 → Not only ____ he apologise, but he also paid for the damage.
sentences.english: 他不仅道了歉，还赔偿了损失。
sentences.referenceExample: Not only **did** he apologise, but he also paid for the damage.

sentences.sentence: 她刚说完，观众就鼓起掌来。 → No sooner ____ she finished than the audience applauded.
sentences.english: 她刚说完，观众就鼓起掌来。
sentences.referenceExample: No sooner **had** she finished than the audience applauded.

sentences.sentence: 我做梦也没想到会赢。 → Never ____ I dream of winning.
直到很久以后我们才知道真相。 → Only much later ____ we learn the truth.
sentences.english: 直到很久以后我们才知道真相。
sentences.referenceExample: Only much later **did** we learn the truth.

sentences.sentence: 他很少在公众场合讲话。 → Seldom ____ he speak in public.
sentences.english: 他很少在公众场合讲话。

sentences.sentence: 任何情况下都不得泄露密码。 → Under no circumstances ____ the password be shared.
sentences.english: 任何情况下都不得泄露密码。
sentences.referenceExample: Under no circumstances **must** the password be shared.

quizzes.title: 条件句的倒装（省略 if）

help.intro: 正式条件句可以省略 if，改用倒装。

tips.title: Had / Were / Should 开头
tips.text: Had I known… = If I had known…；Were I… = If I were…；Should you… = If you should…。

subjects.display: 要是我早知道，就会帮你。
万一你需要帮助，打给我。
要是没有你的帮助，我们就失败了。
万一计划有变，我们会通知您。
要是我当时在场，我就阻止了。
如果我处在她的位置，我会接受。
要是他们早点动身，就不会误机了。
万一下雨，活动将移到室内。
如果不是价格太高，我们就买了。
万一您需要更多信息，请访问我们的网站。
要是我听了她的建议，就成功了。
如果这属实，后果将很严重。
要是他们做了准备，就不会那么慌了。
万一航班取消，您将获得全额退款。

sentences.sentence: 要是我早知道，就会帮你。 → ____ I known, I would have helped.
sentences.english: 要是我早知道，就会帮你。
sentences.referenceExample: **Had** I known, I would have helped.

sentences.sentence: 如果我是你，我会拒绝。 → ____ I you, I would refuse.
万一你需要帮助，打给我。 → ____ you need help, call me.
sentences.english: 万一你需要帮助，打给我。

sentences.sentence: 要是没有你的帮助，我们就失败了。 → Had it not been for your help, we ____ have failed.
sentences.english: 要是没有你的帮助，我们就失败了。
sentences.referenceExample: Had it not been for your help, we **would** have failed.

sentences.sentence: 万一计划有变，我们会通知您。 → ____ the plan change, we will inform you.
sentences.english: 万一计划有变，我们会通知您。
sentences.referenceExample: **Should** the plan change, we will inform you.

sentences.sentence: 要是我当时在场，我就阻止了。 → ____ I been there, I would have stopped it.
sentences.english: 要是我当时在场，我就阻止了。
sentences.referenceExample: **Had** I been there, I would have stopped it.

sentences.sentence: 如果我处在她的位置，我会接受。 → ____ I in her position, I would accept.
sentences.english: 如果我处在她的位置，我会接受。
sentences.referenceExample: **Were** I in her position, I would accept.

sentences.sentence: 要是他们早点动身，就不会误机了。 → Had they left earlier, they ____ not have missed the flight.
sentences.english: 要是他们早点动身，就不会误机了。
sentences.referenceExample: Had they left earlier, they **would** not have missed the flight.

sentences.sentence: 万一下雨，活动将移到室内。 → ____ it rain, the event will move indoors.
sentences.english: 万一下雨，活动将移到室内。
sentences.referenceExample: **Should** it rain, the event will move indoors.

sentences.sentence: 如果不是价格太高，我们就买了。 → ____ the price not been so high, we would have bought it.
sentences.english: 如果不是价格太高，我们就买了。
sentences.referenceExample: **Had** the price not been so high, we would have bought it.

sentences.sentence: 万一您需要更多信息，请访问我们的网站。 → ____ you require further information, please visit our website.
sentences.english: 万一您需要更多信息，请访问我们的网站。
sentences.referenceExample: **Should** you require further information, please visit our website.

sentences.sentence: 要是我听了她的建议，就成功了。 → ____ I followed her advice, I would have succeeded.
sentences.english: 要是我听了她的建议，就成功了。
sentences.referenceExample: **Had** I followed her advice, I would have succeeded.

sentences.sentence: 如果这属实，后果将很严重。 → ____ this true, the consequences would be serious.
sentences.english: 如果这属实，后果将很严重。
sentences.referenceExample: **Were** this true, the consequences would be serious.

sentences.sentence: 要是他们做了准备，就不会那么慌了。 → ____ they prepared, they would not have panicked.
sentences.english: 要是他们做了准备，就不会那么慌了。
sentences.referenceExample: **Had** they prepared, they would not have panicked.

sentences.sentence: 万一航班取消，您将获得全额退款。 → ____ the flight be cancelled, you will receive a full refund.
sentences.english: 万一航班取消，您将获得全额退款。
sentences.referenceExample: **Should** the flight be cancelled, you will receive a full refund.

help.intro: 把想强调的成分提到句首，让语气更有力，有时会引起倒装。

tips.title: ⚠️ 主题前置（Z22）
tips.text: 源自中文的主题句：把强调的部分提前——Money I don't have; time I **do**。

subjects.display: 这样的错误绝不能重犯。
山谷中坐落着一座小村庄。
他说的话我一个字都不信。

这个问题我们稍后再谈。（前置宾语）
钟声响起，随之而来的是一片寂静。
如此重要的决定，我们不能仓促做出。

sentences.sentence: 这样的错误绝不能重犯。 → Such mistakes ____ never be repeated.
sentences.english: 这样的错误绝不能重犯。

sentences.referenceExample: Money I don't have; time I **do**.

山顶上矗立着一座古塔。 → On the hilltop ____ an ancient tower.
sentences.english: 山顶上矗立着一座古塔。

sentences.english: 树林深处藏着一间小木屋。
sentences.referenceExample: Deep in the woods **stood** a little cabin.

sentences.sentence: 这个问题我们稍后再谈。（前置宾语） → This question we will ____ later.
sentences.english: 这个问题我们稍后再谈。（前置宾语）

sentences.sentence: 钟声响起，随之而来的是一片寂静。 → The bell rang, and then ____ the silence.
sentences.english: 钟声响起，随之而来的是一片寂静。
sentences.referenceExample: The bell rang, and then **came** the silence.

sentences.sentence: 如此重要的决定，我们不能仓促做出。 → So important a decision we cannot ____ in haste.
sentences.english: 如此重要的决定，我们不能仓促做出。

sentences.sentence: 正前方矗立着大教堂。 → Straight ahead ____ the cathedral.

quizzes.title: 开口说：正式与非正式语体

help.intro: 同一个意思，正式和非正式场合说法不同。听并跟读，感受差异。

tips.title: 语体的选择（Z32）
tips.text: 正式场合更委婉、更间接：Would you like me to assist you? vs Need a hand?

phrases.text: Would you like me to assist you?
I'm afraid that won't be possible.
I was wondering if you could help me.

help.intro: 学术和正式英语常用模糊限制语来软化语气、避免绝对化。

tips.title: ⚠️ 别太绝对（Z31）
tips.text: tend to / appear to / arguably / to some extent 让论断更谨慎。中文更直接，注意补上这层委婉。

subjects.display: 这在某种程度上是对的。

sentences.sentence: 这在某种程度上是对的。 → This is, to some ____, true.

sentences.sentence: 似乎有个误会。 → There ____ to be a misunderstanding.

sentences.referenceExample: The data **seems** to support this view.

在多数情况下，这个方法有效。 → In ____ cases, this method works.
sentences.english: 在多数情况下，这个方法有效。

sentences.english: 结果在一定程度上取决于运气。
sentences.referenceExample: The outcome depends, to a certain **extent**, on luck.

sentences.sentence: 证据表明（似乎表明）存在联系。 → The evidence ____ a connection.
sentences.english: 证据表明（似乎表明）存在联系。

sentences.sentence: 这大体上是正确的。 → This is ____ correct.
结果可能因人而异。 → Results may ____ from person to person.
sentences.referenceExample: Results may **vary** from person to person.

sentences.sentence: 据我们所知，这是首例。 → As far as we ____, this is the first case.
sentences.referenceExample: As far as we **know**, this is the first case.

sentences.sentence: 这个说法似乎有些夸张。 → The claim ____ somewhat exaggerated.
sentences.english: 这个说法似乎有些夸张。

help.intro: 用 It is said that… / 主语 + be + 过去分词 + to do 客观转述，不点名消息来源。

tips.title: 两种句型
tips.text: It is said/believed that…；或 He is thought/said to be…。常见于新闻和学术。

subjects.display: 人们认为运动有益健康。
据报道事故发生在夜里。
据信这幅画已有三百年历史。
据说那家公司陷入了困境。
据了解双方已达成协议。
据称该公司隐瞒了亏损。
普遍认为锻炼能改善情绪。
这座桥据说是本地最古老的。

sentences.sentence: 据说他很有钱。 → It is ____ that he is rich.
sentences.referenceExample: It is **said** that he is rich.

sentences.sentence: 人们认为运动有益健康。 → Exercise is ____ to be good for health.
sentences.english: 人们认为运动有益健康。
sentences.referenceExample: Exercise is **thought** to be good for health.

sentences.sentence: 据报道事故发生在夜里。 → The accident is ____ to have happened at night.
sentences.english: 据报道事故发生在夜里。
sentences.referenceExample: The accident is **reported** to have happened at night.

sentences.sentence: 大家普遍相信…… → It is widely ____ that ...
他被认为是最佳人选。 → He is ____ to be the best candidate.
sentences.referenceExample: He is **considered** to be the best candidate.

sentences.sentence: 据信这幅画已有三百年历史。 → The painting is ____ to be three hundred years old.
sentences.english: 据信这幅画已有三百年历史。

sentences.sentence: 据说那家公司陷入了困境。 → The company is ____ to be in trouble.
sentences.english: 据说那家公司陷入了困境。
sentences.referenceExample: The company is **said** to be in trouble.

sentences.sentence: 据估计有上千人参加。 → It is ____ that a thousand people attended.
sentences.referenceExample: It is **estimated** that a thousand people attended.

sentences.sentence: 他被传闻已经辞职。 → He is ____ to have resigned.
据预计价格会上涨。 → It is ____ that prices will rise.
sentences.referenceExample: It is **expected** that prices will rise.

sentences.sentence: 据了解双方已达成协议。 → It is ____ that both sides have reached an agreement.
sentences.english: 据了解双方已达成协议。
sentences.referenceExample: It is **understood** that both sides have reached an agreement.

sentences.sentence: 他被认为已离开该国。 → He is ____ to have left the country.
sentences.referenceExample: He is **thought** to have left the country.

sentences.sentence: 据称该公司隐瞒了亏损。 → The company is ____ to have hidden its losses.
sentences.english: 据称该公司隐瞒了亏损。
sentences.referenceExample: The company is **alleged** to have hidden its losses.

sentences.sentence: 普遍认为锻炼能改善情绪。 → It is generally ____ that exercise improves mood.
sentences.english: 普遍认为锻炼能改善情绪。
sentences.referenceExample: It is generally **accepted** that exercise improves mood.

sentences.sentence: 这座桥据说是本地最古老的。 → The bridge is ____ to be the oldest in the area.
sentences.english: 这座桥据说是本地最古老的。
sentences.referenceExample: The bridge is **said** to be the oldest in the area.

quizzes.title: 听力：A political interview

help.intro: 先听，再答题。政治访谈中大量使用委婉和习语。

tips.title: 委婉 + 习语（Z31/Z32）
tips.text: I would say、too early to judge（委婉）；Rome wasn't built in a day（习语）；What I would ask…（强调句）。

quizzes.passage: Minister, thank you for joining us. Critics say your new housing policy has failed. How do you respond? — Well, I would say it's too early to judge. It is true that progress has been slower than we hoped. However, we've laid the foundations for long-term change. — But families are still waiting for homes. — I understand their frustration, and I share it. What I would ask is for a little more patience. Rome, as they say, wasn't built in a day. — Minister, thank you.
quizzes.passageTranslation: 部长，感谢您接受采访。批评者说您的新住房政策失败了，您怎么回应？——嗯，我会说现在下结论还为时过早。诚然，进展比我们希望的要慢。然而，我们已经为长期变革打下了基础。——但families仍在等待住房。——我理解他们的沮丧，我也感同身受。我想请求的是多一点耐心。正如人们所说，罗马不是一天建成的。——部长，谢谢您。

questions.question: How does the minister respond to criticism?

help.intro: 用 nonetheless、moreover、by contrast 等连接观点，让论述更有条理、更正式。

tips.title: 连接词的功能
tips.text: nonetheless（尽管如此）、moreover（此外）、by contrast（相比之下）、in other words（换言之）。

subjects.display: 尽管如此，我们仍需谨慎。
相比之下，第二种方案更便宜。
也就是说，需要更多时间。
同样地，第二个实验也失败了。
总而言之，改革势在必行。
此外，成本也是一个因素。
就此而言，两个方案是相同的。（in this respect）
综上所述，该提案值得支持。
与此同时，成本持续上升。
更重要的是，数据是可靠的。
换个角度说，问题在于信任。

sentences.sentence: 尽管如此，我们仍需谨慎。 → ____, we must be cautious.
sentences.english: 尽管如此，我们仍需谨慎。

sentences.sentence: 此外，还有其他因素。 → ____, there are other factors.

quizzes.title: 阅读：An opinion column

help.intro: 读一篇观点专栏。留意修辞、倒装和习语式的表达。

tips.title: 修辞语体
tips.text: so too does thought（倒装）；We would do well to…（委婉建议）；排比与对比增强说服力。

quizzes.passage: There is a growing tendency, especially among politicians, to speak in slogans rather than substance. Complex problems are reduced to three-word phrases, as if a catchy rhyme could solve a housing crisis or repair a broken health service. This, I would argue, is not merely lazy; it is dangerous. When language becomes empty, so too does thought. A society that stops demanding careful argument will, sooner or later, stop receiving it. We would do well to remember that the loudest voice is rarely the wisest, and that a simple answer to a difficult question is almost always the wrong one.
quizzes.passageTranslation: 有一种日益增长的倾向，尤其在政客中间：说口号，而非实质。复杂的问题被简化成三字短语，仿佛一句朗朗上口的顺口溜就能解决住房危机或修复崩坏的医疗系统。我要说，这不仅仅是懒惰，更是危险。当语言变得空洞，思想也随之空洞。一个不再要求缜密论证的社会，迟早也将不再得到缜密论证。我们最好记住：最大的嗓门很少是最智慧的，而对难题给出的简单答案，几乎总是错的。

quizzes.title: 听力：A business negotiation

help.intro: 先听，再答题。留意谈判中的委婉条件句和使役结构。

tips.title: 条件 + 使役
tips.text: If you could reduce…we'd be prepared（委婉条件）；have the contract drawn up（使役被动）。

quizzes.passage: Thank you for meeting us. Let me be direct: we're very interested in your product, but the price is a concern. — I appreciate your honesty. What did you have in mind? — If you could reduce the price by ten per cent, we'd be prepared to sign a two-year contract. — That's a significant reduction. However, for a two-year commitment, I think we could offer eight per cent. — Let's say nine, and we have a deal. — Nine it is. I'll have the contract drawn up.
quizzes.passageTranslation: 感谢与我们会面。我就直说了：我们对贵方的产品很感兴趣，但价格是个顾虑。——感谢您的坦诚。您有什么想法？——如果您能把价格降低百分之十，我们愿意签一份两年的合同。——这个降幅可不小。不过，考虑到两年的承诺，我想我们可以让百分之八。——就九个点吧，成交。——那就九个点。我这就让人把合同拟好。

quizzes.title: 阅读：Two reviews, two registers

help.intro: 读两则语体截然不同的评价。本课的核心：语体意识。

tips.title: 语体对比（Z32）
tips.text: 正式：exquisite、considerable skill；非正式：well nice、defo、lol。流利 = 会在对的场合用对的语体。

quizzes.passage: Here are two reviews of the same restaurant. The first, from a food critic, reads: 'The dishes, though modest in appearance, reveal a chef of considerable skill; the balance of flavours is, quite frankly, exquisite.' The second, posted online by a customer, says: 'Food was well nice! A bit pricey but worth it lol. Will defo go back!' Both reviews are positive, yet they could hardly be more different. The first uses careful, formal language; the second is casual and full of slang. Neither is 'wrong'. Rather, each is appropriate to its context — and knowing which register to use, and when, is one of the true marks of fluency.
quizzes.passageTranslation: 这里有对同一家餐厅的两则评价。第一则出自美食评论家：「这些菜肴外表朴素，却显露出一位技艺不凡的厨师；风味的平衡，坦白说，堪称精妙。」第二则由一位顾客发在网上：「东西超好吃！有点小贵但值了 哈哈。绝对还会再去！」两则都是好评，却几乎再不同不过。前者用词讲究、正式；后者随意，满是俚语。两者都没有「错」。相反，各自都契合其语境——而知道该在何时使用哪种语体，正是真正流利的标志之一。

quizzes.title: 听力：Irony & humour

help.intro: 先听，再答题。关键是听出反讽——说的和真正的意思相反。

tips.title: ⚠️ 反讽（Z31）
tips.text: 'Truly, we are living in the future' 是反讽：字面在夸，实则在讽刺。靠语气和上下文判断。

quizzes.passage: So, I bought one of those 'smart' home devices last month. You know, the ones that are supposed to make your life easier. Well, let me tell you how my morning went. I asked it to turn on the lights. It played jazz. I asked it to play music. It ordered fifty rolls of toilet paper. And when I finally, in desperation, shouted 'Help!', it cheerfully replied: 'I'm sorry, I didn't quite catch that.' Truly, we are living in the future.
quizzes.passageTranslation: 话说，我上个月买了那种「智能」家居设备。你懂的，就是号称能让生活更轻松的那种。来，让我说说我那天早上过得怎么样。我叫它开灯，它放起了爵士乐。我叫它放音乐，它订了五十卷厕纸。最后我绝望地喊「救命！」，它欢快地回答：「抱歉，我没太听清。」我们，真是活在未来啊。

questions.question: What is the speaker really saying about the device?
questions.questionTranslation: 说话人其实在说这个设备怎么样？

questions.question: Is the speaker being serious at the end?

help.intro: 用助动词 do、强调句和否定倒装突出信息、加强语气。

quizzes.title: 阅读：A satirical article

help.intro: 读一篇讽刺文章。关键是识别夸张背后的讽刺，别当真。

tips.title: ⚠️ 讽刺文体（Z31）
tips.text: 用荒诞的夸张来批评现实观点（「快乐是简单的选择」）。识别出它并非字面真实。

quizzes.passage: In a bold move to improve public health, the government has announced that from next year, all citizens will be required to feel happy at all times. Frowning in public will carry a small fine, while excessive sighing may result in a mandatory 'joy workshop'. A spokesperson explained: 'We believe happiness is a simple choice. If people are unhappy, it is clearly their own fault.' Critics have pointed out that poverty, stress and poor healthcare might have something to do with it — but such negativity, the government insists, is exactly the problem. The scheme will be funded by a new tax on umbrellas, since rain, too, has been declared unpatriotic.
quizzes.passageTranslation: 为改善公众健康，政府大胆宣布：从明年起，全体公民必须时刻感到快乐。在公共场合皱眉将被处以小额罚款，而过度叹气可能被强制参加「快乐工作坊」。一位发言人解释道：「我们认为快乐是一个简单的选择。如果人们不快乐，那显然是他们自己的错。」批评者指出，贫困、压力和糟糕的医疗或许与此有关——但政府坚称，这种消极情绪正是问题所在。该计划将由一项新的雨伞税提供资金，因为下雨也已被宣布为不爱国。

questions.questionTranslation: 这篇文章在描述真实政策吗？

quizzes.title: 听力：A literary reading

help.intro: 先听，再答题。留意营造氛围的文学手法。

tips.title: 文学手法（Z31）
tips.text: 拟人（windows seemed to follow you）、氛围营造、留白——不解释反而更有力。

quizzes.passage: Listen to this short passage. 'The old house stood at the end of the lane, silent and watchful, as it had for a hundred years. Its windows, dark and empty, seemed to follow you as you passed. The villagers said nothing lived there now — nothing, at least, that they cared to name. But on winter nights, when the wind was still, a single light would sometimes appear in the highest window, and then, just as quickly, be gone.' Notice how the writer creates a feeling of mystery without ever explaining what is really there.
quizzes.passageTranslation: 听这一小段文字：「那座老屋伫立在小巷尽头，沉默而警觉，一如它百年来的模样。它那一扇扇黑洞洞、空荡荡的窗户，似乎在你经过时目送着你。村民说如今那里什么都不住了——至少，没有他们愿意说出名字的东西。可在冬夜，风止之时，最高的那扇窗里有时会亮起一盏孤灯，随即，又同样迅速地熄灭。」注意作者如何在从不解释的情况下营造神秘感。

questions.question: What kind of text is this?
What feeling does the writer create?
Does the writer explain the light?

help.intro: 听句子并打出来。注意委婉、倒装、强调句等细腻结构。

tips.title: ⚠️ 细腻结构（Z31）
tips.text: 写出 not so much…as…、Had we…、to put it mildly、What matters is…。

items.text: One could argue that the opposite is true.
items.translation: 有人可能会说恰恰相反。

items.text: It is not so much a problem as a symptom.
items.translation: 与其说这是问题，不如说是症状。

items.text: Had we acted sooner, this might have been avoided.
items.translation: 要是我们早点行动，也许本可避免。

items.text: The evidence is, to put it mildly, unconvincing.
items.translation: 委婉地说，这些证据缺乏说服力。

items.text: What matters is not what we say, but what we do.
items.translation: 重要的不是我们说什么，而是做什么。

items.text: Rarely has this assumption been questioned.
items.translation: 很少有人质疑这一假设。

items.text: The plan is by no means perfect, but it is worth trying.
items.translation: 这个方案绝非完美，但值得一试。

items.text: It is this silence that worries people.
items.translation: 正是这种沉默让人担忧。

items.text: Caution, as it turned out, was justified.
He should have thought twice before acting.
The decision was hasty, to say the least.
items.translation: 这个决定说好听点也是仓促的。

items.text: Never have we been given a full explanation.
items.translation: 我们从来没有得到过完整的解释。（否定倒装）

items.text: What counts is not speed but direction.
items.translation: 关键不在速度，而在方向。

items.text: The criticism, though harsh, was not without merit.
items.translation: 批评虽严厉，却并非没有道理。

items.text: With a little more patience, the outcome might have been different.
items.translation: 要是当时多一点耐心，结果也许会不同。

quizzes.title: 阅读：A book review with irony

help.intro: 读一篇带反讽的书评。留意「明褒暗贬」的手法。

tips.title: 明褒暗贬（Z32）
tips.text: 'towering achievement' → 转为吐槽篇幅；'something shorter' 是含蓄的贬评。识别反语与低调陈述。

quizzes.passage: Mr Pinter's new novel, we are told, is a 'towering achievement'. It is certainly towering in length: at nine hundred pages, it could comfortably serve as a doorstop. The plot, such as it is, follows a middle-aged professor who spends the entire book deciding whether or not to buy a new hat. Along the way, we are treated to forty pages on the history of felt. Admirers will call this 'meditative'; the rest of us may call it something shorter. And yet — I confess — I read to the end. Perhaps, buried beneath the endless description, there is a real story struggling to get out. Or perhaps I simply wanted to know about the hat.
quizzes.passageTranslation: 据说，Pinter 先生的新小说是一部「巍峨的杰作」。它在篇幅上确实巍峨：九百页，完全可以当门挡用。至于情节——如果那也算情节的话——讲的是一位中年教授用整本书来纠结要不要买一顶新帽子。一路上，我们还「有幸」读到四十页关于毡子历史的内容。仰慕者会称之为「冥想式」；我们其余人也许会用一个更短的词来形容。然而——我承认——我读到了最后。也许，在无尽的描写之下，真有一个故事在挣扎着想冒出来。又或者，我只是想知道那顶帽子到底怎样了。

questions.questionTranslation: 评论者真正的看法是什么？

help.intro: 用衔接短语把段落织成整体，让论述层层推进。

tips.title: 衔接手段（Z31）
tips.text: coupled with、that said、as noted、for this reason、in sum——高级语篇的黏合剂。

subjects.display: 这一点，再加上前述，解释了失败。
出于这个原因，我们停了下来。
与此密切相关的是成本问题。
鉴于上述情况，我们建议……
反过来，这又引发了新问题。
话虽如此，风险依然存在。
就此而论，两个案例十分相似。
基于同样的理由，我们反对该提案。
综合考虑各方面因素，方案 B 更佳。

sentences.sentence: 这一点，再加上前述，解释了失败。 → This, ____ with the above, explains the failure.
sentences.english: 这一点，再加上前述，解释了失败。
sentences.referenceExample: This, **coupled** with the above, explains the failure.

sentences.sentence: 正如前所述…… → As ____ earlier, ...
出于这个原因，我们停了下来。 → For this ____, we stopped.
sentences.english: 出于这个原因，我们停了下来。

sentences.sentence: 话虽如此，仍有希望。 → That ____, there is still hope.
如前几段所示…… → As the previous paragraphs ____, ...
与此密切相关的是成本问题。 → Closely ____ to this is the question of cost.
sentences.english: 与此密切相关的是成本问题。
sentences.referenceExample: Closely **related** to this is the question of cost.

sentences.sentence: 鉴于上述情况，我们建议…… → In ____ of the above, we recommend ...
sentences.english: 鉴于上述情况，我们建议……
sentences.referenceExample: In **light** of the above, we recommend ...

sentences.sentence: 反过来，这又引发了新问题。 → This, in ____, raises new questions.
sentences.english: 反过来，这又引发了新问题。

sentences.sentence: 话虽如此，风险依然存在。 → That ____, the risks remain.
sentences.english: 话虽如此，风险依然存在。

sentences.sentence: 如下文所示…… → As will be ____ below, ...
就此而论，两个案例十分相似。 → In this ____, the two cases are very similar.
sentences.english: 就此而论，两个案例十分相似。
sentences.referenceExample: In this **regard**, the two cases are very similar.

sentences.sentence: 基于同样的理由，我们反对该提案。 → By the same ____, we oppose the proposal.
sentences.english: 基于同样的理由，我们反对该提案。
sentences.referenceExample: By the same **token**, we oppose the proposal.

sentences.sentence: 简而言之，代价太高了。 → In ____, the cost is too high.
sentences.referenceExample: In **short**, the cost is too high.

sentences.sentence: 综合考虑各方面因素，方案 B 更佳。 → All things ____, option B is better.
sentences.english: 综合考虑各方面因素，方案 B 更佳。
sentences.referenceExample: All things **considered**, option B is better.

help.intro: 排比、对偶、低调陈述等修辞让语言更有感染力。

tips.title: 修辞（Z31）
tips.text: 排比（I came, I saw, I conquered）、低调陈述（no small matter = 大事）、对比。

subjects.display: 我来了，我看见了，我征服了。
问题不是要不要，而是何时。
问问你能为国家做什么。（对偶）
这不是结束，甚至不是结束的开始。
轻描淡写：这有点小贵。（其实很贵）
排比：政府民有、民治、民享。
低调陈述：他对结果不太满意。（其实很生气）
对比：我们要的是桥梁，不是高墙。
反问：我们还要再等多少年？
三段排比：更快、更高、更强。

sentences.sentence: 我来了，我看见了，我征服了。 → I came, I saw, I ____.
sentences.english: 我来了，我看见了，我征服了。

sentences.sentence: 这可不是小事。 → This is ____ small matter.
问题不是要不要，而是何时。 → The question is not ____, but when.
sentences.english: 问题不是要不要，而是何时。
sentences.referenceExample: The question is not **whether**, but when.

sentences.sentence: 要么现在，要么永不。 → It is now or ____.
不自由，毋宁死。 → Give me liberty, or give me ____.
sentences.referenceExample: Give me liberty, or give me **death**.

sentences.sentence: 问问你能为国家做什么。（对偶） → Ask ____ you can do for your country.
sentences.english: 问问你能为国家做什么。（对偶）
sentences.referenceExample: Ask **what** you can do for your country.

sentences.sentence: 说来容易，做来难。 → Easier said than ____.
这不是结束，甚至不是结束的开始。 → This is not the end, nor even the beginning of the ____.
sentences.english: 这不是结束，甚至不是结束的开始。
sentences.referenceExample: This is not the end, nor even the beginning of the **end**.

sentences.sentence: 轻描淡写：这有点小贵。（其实很贵） → It is a ____ on the expensive side.
sentences.english: 轻描淡写：这有点小贵。（其实很贵）
sentences.referenceExample: It is a **little** on the expensive side.

sentences.sentence: 我们越少谈论它越好。 → The less said about it, the ____.
sentences.referenceExample: The less said about it, the **better**.

sentences.sentence: 排比：政府民有、民治、民享。 → Government of the people, by the people, for the ____.
sentences.english: 排比：政府民有、民治、民享。
sentences.referenceExample: Government of the people, by the people, for the **people**.

sentences.sentence: 低调陈述：他对结果不太满意。（其实很生气） → He was ____ exactly pleased with the result.
sentences.english: 低调陈述：他对结果不太满意。（其实很生气）
sentences.referenceExample: He was **not** exactly pleased with the result.

sentences.sentence: 对比：我们要的是桥梁，不是高墙。 → We want bridges, not ____.
sentences.english: 对比：我们要的是桥梁，不是高墙。

sentences.sentence: 反问：我们还要再等多少年？ → How many more years must we ____?
sentences.english: 反问：我们还要再等多少年？
sentences.referenceExample: How many more years must we **wait**?

sentences.sentence: 三段排比：更快、更高、更强。 → Faster, higher, ____.
sentences.english: 三段排比：更快、更高、更强。

help.intro: 用倒装、even、were it not for、unless 等表达最细腻的假设。

tips.title: 高级条件（Z28）
tips.text: Even had we…、Were it not for…、Had… been…、Unless stated otherwise。

subjects.display: 即便当时更努力，结果也可能一样。
要不是因为他，我们早失败了。
除非另有说明，规则照旧。
就算给我一百万我也不干。
倘若价格再高一点，市场早就崩溃了。
要不是运气好，一切都会不同。
即便有再多的钱，也买不回时间。
除非有相反的证据，我们维持原判断。
万一情况有变，请立即通知我们。
要不是那场雨，收成早就毁了。
即便再给一次机会，他也会做同样的选择。
除非另行通知，会议照常举行。
假如换一个时代，她也许早已成名。
倘若当时有人反对，计划就会被搁置。

sentences.sentence: 即便当时更努力，结果也可能一样。 → Even had we tried harder, the result ____ have been the same.
sentences.english: 即便当时更努力，结果也可能一样。
sentences.referenceExample: Even had we tried harder, the result **might** have been the same.

sentences.sentence: 要不是因为他，我们早失败了。 → Were it not for him, we would have ____.
sentences.english: 要不是因为他，我们早失败了。
sentences.referenceExample: Were it not for him, we would have **failed**.

sentences.sentence: 假如历史稍有不同…… → Had history been ____ different, ...
除非另有说明，规则照旧。 → Unless ____ otherwise, the rules apply.
sentences.english: 除非另有说明，规则照旧。

sentences.sentence: 就算给我一百万我也不干。 → I wouldn't do it, not ____ for a million.
sentences.english: 就算给我一百万我也不干。
sentences.referenceExample: I wouldn't do it, not **even** for a million.

sentences.sentence: 倘若价格再高一点，市场早就崩溃了。 → Had prices risen any higher, the market ____ have collapsed.
sentences.english: 倘若价格再高一点，市场早就崩溃了。
sentences.referenceExample: Had prices risen any higher, the market **would** have collapsed.

sentences.sentence: 要不是运气好，一切都会不同。 → Were it not for luck, everything would have been ____.
sentences.english: 要不是运气好，一切都会不同。
sentences.referenceExample: Were it not for luck, everything would have been **different**.

sentences.sentence: 即便有再多的钱，也买不回时间。 → Even with all the money in the world, you ____ buy back time.
sentences.english: 即便有再多的钱，也买不回时间。
sentences.referenceExample: Even with all the money in the world, you **couldn't** buy back time.

sentences.sentence: 除非有相反的证据，我们维持原判断。 → Unless there is evidence to the ____, our view stands.
sentences.english: 除非有相反的证据，我们维持原判断。
sentences.referenceExample: Unless there is evidence to the **contrary**, our view stands.

sentences.sentence: 万一情况有变，请立即通知我们。 → ____ the situation change, inform us at once.
sentences.english: 万一情况有变，请立即通知我们。
sentences.referenceExample: **Should** the situation change, inform us at once.

sentences.sentence: 要不是那场雨，收成早就毁了。 → Were it not for the rain, the harvest would have been ____.
sentences.english: 要不是那场雨，收成早就毁了。
sentences.referenceExample: Were it not for the rain, the harvest would have been **ruined**.

sentences.sentence: 即便再给一次机会，他也会做同样的选择。 → Even given a second chance, he ____ make the same choice.
sentences.english: 即便再给一次机会，他也会做同样的选择。
sentences.referenceExample: Even given a second chance, he **would** make the same choice.

sentences.sentence: 除非另行通知，会议照常举行。 → Unless otherwise ____, the meeting will go ahead.
sentences.english: 除非另行通知，会议照常举行。
sentences.referenceExample: Unless otherwise **notified**, the meeting will go ahead.

sentences.sentence: 假如换一个时代，她也许早已成名。 → In another era, she ____ have been famous.
sentences.english: 假如换一个时代，她也许早已成名。
sentences.referenceExample: In another era, she **might** have been famous.

sentences.sentence: 倘若当时有人反对，计划就会被搁置。 → Had anyone objected, the plan ____ have been shelved.
sentences.english: 倘若当时有人反对，计划就会被搁置。
sentences.referenceExample: Had anyone objected, the plan **would** have been shelved.

help.intro: 用排比、停顿和坚定的语调打动听众。听并跟读。

tips.title: 演讲的力量（Z9）
tips.text: 排比、留白、直呼听众、有力的结语——让语言产生感染力。

phrases.text: Friends, today we stand at a crossroads.

help.intro: 隐喻和习语承载文化。地道使用能让表达生动而精准。

tips.title: ⚠️ 文化的结晶（Z32）
tips.text: a double-edged sword（双刃剑）、the elephant in the room（谁都不愿谈的问题）、a blessing in disguise（因祸得福）。

压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草 → the last ____

sentences.english: 亡羊补牢，为时未晚（迟做总比不做好）

help.intro: 讣告的庄重、打趣的轻松、外交的含蓄——高级表达在于分寸。

tips.title: 分寸（Z32）
tips.text: 不同场合选择恰当的语气：庄重、含蓄、真诚或调侃，都靠固定表达来实现。

sentences.sentence: 庄重宣布（讣告语气） → It is with deep regret that we ____ ...

外交辞令 → We have agreed to ____.

quizzes.title: 听力：A current-affairs debate

help.intro: 先听，再答题。留意双方的修辞和论证。

tips.title: 辩论修辞（Z31）
tips.text: 'a slow poison'（隐喻）；'give a voice to the voiceless'（对比排比）；正反论点均衡。

quizzes.passage: Tonight's motion: 'This house believes that social media does more harm than good.' Speaking for the motion: 'We have created a world in which teenagers compare their real lives to the edited highlights of others, and then wonder why they feel inadequate. That is not connection; it is a slow poison.' And against: 'Every new technology has been feared. Social media has given a voice to the voiceless and toppled dictators. To blame the tool for how some use it is both lazy and dangerous.' A powerful exchange. Now, over to our audience.
quizzes.passageTranslation: 今晚的辩题：「本方认为社交媒体弊大于利。」正方发言：「我们造就了这样一个世界：青少年拿自己真实的生活去和别人经过修饰的高光片段比较，然后纳闷自己为何感到不如人。那不是连接，而是一种慢性毒药。」反方：「每一项新技术都曾被恐惧。社交媒体给了无声者以声音，也曾推翻独裁者。因为有些人的滥用就去责怪工具本身，既懒惰又危险。」精彩的交锋。现在，交给现场观众。

questions.question: What is the debate motion?
options: Social media does more harm than good

quizzes.title: 阅读：A journalistic analysis

help.intro: 读一篇分析性新闻评论。留意数据背后的批判视角。

tips.title: 分析性写作（Z31）
tips.text: 'Look closer, however'（转折）；委婉限定（rarely the whole truth）；'The real question is…'（强调句）。

quizzes.passage: The numbers, at first glance, tell a reassuring story: unemployment is at a record low. Politicians have, predictably, rushed to take the credit. Look closer, however, and the picture grows murkier. Much of this 'employment' consists of insecure, part-time work, often paying less than a living wage. A person delivering parcels for twelve hours a day, with no sick pay and no guaranteed hours, counts in the statistics as 'employed' — and yet may be poorer than someone officially out of work a decade ago. Statistics, as ever, are not lies; but they are rarely the whole truth. The real question is not how many people are working, but whether that work allows them to live with dignity.
quizzes.passageTranslation: 乍看之下，数字讲述着一个令人安心的故事：失业率处于历史低位。不出所料，政客们争相邀功。然而，凑近一看，图景就变得模糊。许多所谓的「就业」是不稳定的兼职，报酬常常低于维生工资。一个每天送十二小时快递、没有病假、也没有保障工时的人，在统计里算作「就业」——却可能比十年前一个正式失业的人还要穷。数字，一如既往，并非谎言；但它们很少是全部真相。真正的问题不在于有多少人在工作，而在于那份工作能否让他们有尊严地生活。

questions.question: What do the headline numbers suggest?
What is the writer's real point?
questions.questionTranslation: 作者真正的观点是什么？

questions.question: What does the writer say about statistics?
options: Not lies, but not the whole truth

quizzes.title: 复杂被动与非人称结构

help.intro: 高级被动包括 be believed to do、be being done、need + V-ing（含被动义）。

tips.title: 高级被动（Z27）
tips.text: be believed/seen to do、be being done（进行被动）、need + V-ing（=need to be done）。

subjects.display: 有人看见他离开了大楼。
这座桥正在维修中。（进行被动）
这些窗户需要清洗。（need + V-ing）
据报道嫌疑人已被逮捕。
这个问题正在被认真研究。
这些规则需要重新审视。（need + V-ing）
他被公认为该领域的权威。

sentences.sentence: 据信许多物种已灭绝。 → Many species are believed to have ____ extinct.
sentences.referenceExample: Many species are believed to have **become** extinct.

sentences.sentence: 有人看见他离开了大楼。 → He was seen to ____ the building.
sentences.english: 有人看见他离开了大楼。
sentences.referenceExample: He was seen to **leave** the building.

sentences.sentence: 这件事亟需处理。 → The matter needs ____.
此事正由他人处理。 → The issue is being dealt ____ by someone else.
sentences.referenceExample: The issue is being dealt **with** by someone else.

sentences.sentence: 据估计损失巨大。 → The losses are estimated to be ____.
sentences.referenceExample: The losses are estimated to be **considerable**.

sentences.sentence: 这座桥正在维修中。（进行被动） → The bridge is ____ repaired.
sentences.english: 这座桥正在维修中。（进行被动）

sentences.sentence: 这些窗户需要清洗。（need + V-ing） → The windows need ____.
sentences.english: 这些窗户需要清洗。（need + V-ing）

sentences.sentence: 据认为他已离开该国。 → He is thought to have ____ the country.
sentences.referenceExample: He is thought to have **left** the country.

quizzes.title: 开口说：即兴论辩与反驳

help.intro: 即兴反驳要礼貌而坚定，用连接语争取思考时间。听并跟读。

tips.title: 反驳的艺术（Z10）
tips.text: 先承认，再转折，最后立论：I take your point, but… On the contrary…。

phrases.text: I take your point, but consider this ...
phrases.translation: 我明白你的意思，但请考虑……
那正好证明了我的观点。

phrases.text: We must draw a distinction here ...
With respect, that simply doesn't hold up.

quizzes.title: 听力：A literary/critical talk

help.intro: 先听，再答题。留意文学评论中的比喻与对偶。

tips.title: 评论修辞（Z31）
tips.text: 对偶（best of times / worst of times）；比喻（leave a door open）；intrigue ≠ confusion 的辨析。

quizzes.passage: What makes a great opening line? Consider the famous first sentence: 'It was the best of times, it was the worst of times.' In just ten words, Dickens captures an entire age of contradiction. A great opening does not merely begin a story; it makes a promise to the reader. It says: trust me, this will be worth your time. Modern writers, under pressure to grab attention, sometimes forget that intrigue is not the same as confusion. The best openings are clear, yet they leave a door slightly open — a question we cannot help but want answered.
quizzes.passageTranslation: 什么造就了精彩的开篇句？想想那句著名的开头：「这是最好的时代，也是最坏的时代。」仅仅十个词，狄更斯就道尽了一个充满矛盾的时代。伟大的开篇不只是开始一个故事，它是对读者的一个承诺，它在说：相信我，这值得你花时间。现代作家在吸引眼球的压力下，有时忘了「引人入胜」不等于「令人困惑」。最好的开篇是清晰的，却留了一道微微敞开的门——一个我们忍不住想知道答案的问题。

questions.question: What is the talk about?
questions.questionTranslation: 这段讲话的主题是什么？

questions.question: What does a great opening do?
options: Makes a promise to the reader

questions.question: What mistake do some modern writers make?
questions.questionTranslation: 一些现代作家犯了什么错误？

help.intro: 听句子并打出来。这些句子综合了倒装、强调句、委婉和反事实。

tips.title: ⚠️ 综合结构（Z31）
tips.text: 写出 Rarely has…（倒装）、What is needed is…（强调句）、Were the government to…（反事实）。

items.text: Rarely has a decision been so widely criticised.
items.translation: 很少有一个决定受到如此广泛的批评。

items.text: What is needed is not more talk, but action.
items.translation: 需要的不是更多空谈，而是行动。

items.text: The consequences, though hard to predict, are unlikely to be minor.
items.translation: 后果虽难预料，但不太可能微不足道。

items.text: Were the government to reconsider, much could still be saved.
items.translation: 倘若政府重新考虑，仍有很多可挽回。

items.text: It is precisely this complacency that alarms me.
items.translation: 正是这种自满让我警觉。

items.text: Only when the crisis came did people begin to care.
items.translation: 直到危机来临，人们才开始重视。

items.text: The talks are believed to be in their final stage.
items.translation: 据信谈判已进入最后阶段。

items.text: It is not so much a policy as a gesture.
items.translation: 这与其说是政策，不如说是姿态。

items.text: That said, reform cannot wait any longer.
items.translation: 话虽如此，改革不能再等。

items.text: What is needed is courage, not slogans.
items.translation: 需要的是勇气，而非口号。

items.text: History will not forgive us if we fail to act.
items.translation: 若不采取行动，历史不会宽恕我们。

items.text: Only at the last moment was the agreement reached.
items.translation: 直到最后一刻，协议才达成。

items.text: Seldom has a reform enjoyed such unanimous support.
items.translation: 很少有改革得到如此一致的支持。

items.text: The problem lies not in resources, but in will.
items.translation: 问题不在资源，而在意愿。

items.text: That said, optimism must be kept within reason.
items.translation: 话虽如此，乐观也要有分寸。

quizzes.title: 阅读：Analysing a short story

help.intro: 读一段关于短篇小说的文学分析。留意「留白」与含蓄的力量。

tips.title: 文学分析（Z31）
tips.text: 被动（nothing is explained, it has been said）；'white space' 的隐喻；含蓄胜过直白。

quizzes.passage: In Hemingway's famous six-word story — 'For sale: baby shoes, never worn' — nothing is explained, and yet everything is felt. The power lies entirely in what is left unsaid. We are not told who is selling the shoes, or why they were never worn; but the reader's imagination fills the silence with loss. This is the essence of great short fiction: it trusts the reader. Rather than describing grief, Hemingway hands us a single object and lets us feel its weight. The best stories, it has been said, are written as much in the white space between the words as in the words themselves.
quizzes.passageTranslation: 在海明威著名的六词小说——「出售：婴儿鞋，从未穿过」——中，什么都没有解释，却什么都感受到了。力量完全在于「没说出口」的部分。我们不知道是谁在卖这双鞋，也不知道它为何从未被穿过；但读者的想象把这段沉默填满了失去。这正是伟大短篇小说的精髓：它信任读者。海明威没有描写悲伤，而是递给我们一件小小的物品，让我们自己去感受它的重量。有人说，最好的故事，写在词与词之间的留白里，不亚于写在词句本身。

questions.question: What is special about the six-word story?
questions.questionTranslation: 这个六词故事特别在哪里？

questions.question: What does great short fiction do?
questions.questionTranslation: 伟大的短篇小说会做什么？

quizzes.title: 阅读：Capstone — A long-form feature

help.intro: 毕业级长篇特写。综合运用隐喻、反讽与节奏，读出言外的深意。

tips.title: 特写文风（Z31/Z32）
tips.text: 'sell it by the weekend / by the hour'（对偶）；'screens murmur'（拟人）；含蓄有力的结语。

quizzes.passage: For most of human history, silence was free and abundant. Today, it has become a luxury. In our cities, the hum of traffic never truly stops; in our homes, screens murmur through the night. We have, without quite deciding to, engineered a world in which quiet is something we must actively seek out — and pay for. Wellness retreats sell it by the weekend; noise-cancelling headphones sell it by the hour. Yet the deeper cost may be one we have barely begun to measure. Studies increasingly suggest that constant noise raises stress, disturbs sleep, and erodes our very capacity to think. Perhaps the most radical act of the coming century will not be to speak louder, but to learn, once again, how to be still.
quizzes.passageTranslation: 在人类历史的大部分时间里，寂静是免费而充裕的。今天，它却成了一种奢侈。在城市里，车流的嗡鸣从未真正停止；在家中，屏幕彻夜低语。我们并未真正下过决心，却造出了这样一个世界：安静成了必须主动去寻找——而且要花钱买——的东西。养生营按周出售它，降噪耳机按小时出售它。然而更深的代价，也许是我们才刚刚开始衡量的。越来越多的研究表明，持续的噪音会增加压力、扰乱睡眠，并侵蚀我们思考的能力本身。也许，下一个世纪最激进的举动，不是把话说得更响，而是重新学会——如何安静下来。

questions.question: What does the writer suggest about noise?
questions.questionTranslation: 作者暗示噪音有什么影响？

questions.question: What is the writer's closing idea?
options: Learning to be still is radical
questions.questionTranslation: 作者结尾的观点是什么？

quizzes.title: 开口说：Capstone — 就复杂议题表达观点

help.intro: 毕业级口语：综合运用观点框架、让步、证据和有力的结语，完成一次完整的论述。

tips.title: 一次完整的论述（Z9）
tips.text: 立场 → 让步 → 证据 → 结论。用坚定而有分寸的语气收束——这是 C2 的标志。

phrases.text: On this issue, my position is clear.
phrases.translation: 关于这个问题，我的立场很明确。

phrases.text: While there is merit on both sides ...
phrases.translation: 虽然双方都有合理之处……

phrases.text: Ultimately, it comes down to what kind of society we want to be.
phrases.translation: 归根结底，这关乎我们想成为怎样的社会。
